clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old male presented with a two-year history of a large verrucous plaque and malodorous purulent discharge on the buttocks, thigh, and scrotum, accompanied by painful/itchy nodules, foul-smelling seropurulent discharge, and systemic symptoms including untreated cough and night sweats. Previous antifungal and antibiotic treatments had failed. A skin biopsy revealed marked pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, epithelioid granulomatous inflammation with caseous necrosis, Langerhans cells, and lymphocytic infiltrates. Acid-fast bacilli (AFB) staining and culture for M. tuberculosis were negative. Based on clinical suspicion and typical histopathological findings, anti-tuberculosis treatment (ATT) was initiated. The skin lesions showed significant improvement within two months and complete resolution after four months of therapy, leaving atrophic scars.
